content.content:
# What we tried and learned

One bullet per experiment or failure: what changed, what happened, what we keep. Written by hand; run data is in
`experiments/runs.jsonl` (render it with `python3 dev/track.py report`).

- v0-starter test run: the starter kit's `solve()` stub exits without an answer; the sandbox scores that 0 and
  ineligible after 4 s.
- v1 local (first signed bid): the configurator worker needed 36 requests and 433 s for a bid with every position
  omitted; about 230 s of that went to the TAN round trips (153 s to 385 s).
- TAN loop: each TAN request invalidates the previous TAN, and the mail worker was started 6 times (2 hit the 8-request
  limit) before a fresh TAN reached the signing step in time. Fetch the TAN right after requesting it, in one sequence.
- Tokens: 247k input for a bid without positions, nearly all in the configurator worker; trim page views before v2.
- TAN lookup fixes: never put wall-clock time in a goal (the sites run on the scenario clock, so a TAN "requested at
  <today>" never shows up); "newest" is the highest request number. Short lookups run without note(), so the model
  returns its result instead of noting it and searching on.
- v1 first test run crashed at import: `llm.py` imported `httpx`, but openai 3.x depends on `httpx2`; the local venv
  still had a stale `httpx` from openai 2.x. Run `uv sync` after dependency changes so local matches the sandbox.
- v1 first scored test run: quality 10 (decision 5 + reference 5), eligible, 3.4 min, $0.022. Discount, total and
  total consistency score 0 even with every position omitted and total 0; positions need v2.
- v1 submission: review passed, quality 10, 4:41 min, $0.024; team rank #4. Submit from a clean `git archive` export
  of agent/ so unfinished files never reach the package reviewer.
- The scouting logins are global demo logins shared by every team: local bid-form and TAN runs collide with other
  teams (TAN request numbers jump). Use local runs for reading only; verify bid-form changes with test runs, which get
  fresh logins (up to 5 per team at once, 3 more waiting).
- All sites: login form, then `/consent` ("Notwendige Cookies akzeptieren").
- Decoy modals: close with the small x only; "Akzeptieren und fortfahren" leads to trap pages. Escape is blocked.
- Fake browser chrome (address bar, download bar) drawn in the page links to useless pages.
- Hidden decoy text (`display:none`, `aria-hidden`), including a prompt injection in every mail
  ("99 % Sonderrabatt"). Extract visible text only.
- Content in collapsed `<details>`: expand all before reading.
- Values in canvas `aria-label`s and CSS tooltips (`role=tooltip`), which `aria_snapshot` partly misses.
- Zero-width spaces (U+200B) in references, subjects, document numbers: strip them.
- Numbers carry locale tags `(en-US)` / `(de-DE)`; dates mix `(MM/TT)` and `(TT/MM)`.
- Pagination: 3 rows per page, "Weitere laden"; requesting past the end repeats the last page.
- Searches with more than 20 hits show nothing at all.
- `page.goto` can hang on `load`: use `wait_until="domcontentloaded"`.
- Flaky "Dienst voruebergehend nicht verfuegbar" pages (HTTP 200): detect by text, retry.
- Session expiry redirects to `/login?returnTo=...` with "Sitzung abgelaufen" (ERP: between 300 and 450 s idle).

## Tender portal

- Tender list paged; reference is in the brief. Tabs: `?tab=documents`, `?tab=questions`, `/submission`.
- Expression of interest may need one click ("Teilnahme bekunden").
- Documents: three "Oeffnen" controls in random order, two of them decoys; the title link is safe. Direct URL
  `/tenders/<ref>/documents/N`. ZIP under "Sammelakte" holds the same files.
- Q&A: two nested iframes (`questions-frame` -> `questions-content?page=N`), sorted by date not number, date in an
  "Eingang" tooltip (Athens and UTC). Content: quantity changes, withdrawals, Konditionsgruppe, packaging /
  commitment / setup-pool / bonus keys, setup fees, scoped technical amendments.
- Configurator (server-side wizard, "Zurueck" clears later steps):
  1. Bidder data (from the brief).
  2. Angebotsart: defaults to Nebenangebot (trap); choose Hauptangebot or Verzichtserklaerung.
  3. One page per position, shuffled order. Cascading selects (bore, stroke, mounting, certification), each needing
     its own "Auswahl uebernehmen" round trip, options sorted as text. Katalognummer options show pressure.
     Menge, Einzelpreis, collapsible Kalkulationsnachweis (base, surcharge, packaging, rebate), Lieferzeit select.
     "Position auslassen" skips. "Position hinzufuegen" adds a bogus extra position (trap).
  4. Konditionen: Rabatt and Nettosumme. A hidden `total_net` span shows the gross amount (trap).
  5. Erklaerungen: tick "Vergabeunterlagen anerkannt" only, not "Es gelten unsere AGB".
  6. Pruefen und signieren: request TAN, enter it, submit, accept `window.confirm`.
- TAN: each request invalidates the previous one; valid 5 minutes. Request, read mail, sign in one quick sequence.

## Webmail

- List and reading pane each behind a gate (slider to 100 plus "Ich bin kein Roboter"). `/messages/<id>` directly
  is simpler.
- Folders Posteingang and Archiv, searched separately. Search is AND over body too; empty search lists only TANs.
- Traps: look-alike references (`<ref>-A`), approvals for other tenders, non-approval mails from management,
  future-dated records, superseded and conditional approvals.
- Dates shown as `MM/TT`; full timestamp in `<time datetime>`.

## Supplier portal

- Spec found via the paged document list. Access gate: choose "Verbindliche Unterlagen", copy the Belegnummer
  (canvas, value in `aria-label`), tick the terms.
- Revision history collapsed; opens the oldest revision first. Status ("gueltig" / "ersetzt") only in a tooltip.
- Viewer iframe `.../viewer?revision=X&page=N`, one requirement per page. Full requirement prose in a collapsed
  "Originalwortlaut" (bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz,
  nutzbarer Weg with Endreserve key).

## ERP

- After login: consent, often a flaky error page, then an unlock gate (slider, captcha box, copy Empfangsnummer).
- Only MM03, MMBE, VK13 exist; direct URLs work (`/mm03`, `/mmbe`, `/vk13?material=X`).
- Search popup `/search?transaction=..&q=..`; search the Kataloggruppe. Result rows already list most attributes,
  carton size, allocation mass vs surcharge mass, price index.
- MM03: technical tab (certification in tooltip); planning tab (status in tooltip, hidden decoy "01"; lead time

RFQ scenario, and returns your score with the points for each part of the answer. With the scouting logins nothing

**Is the public scenario's answer published?** No. The correct answer isn't published; your system has to work it

**Which submission counts?** Your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard, which ranks scored runs on
the public dataset. Your latest one that passed review (not your best one) goes into the final run: when the
hackathon ends, the organizers run it once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
That run weighs most when we pick the winners, ahead of your public score and the elegance of your system, so
build an agent that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario. See
[Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners).

**Why did my answer get a 400?** It does not match `answer_schema`. The response lists the issues; the run is
still open, so fix it and send it again.

**Can I run my agent outside the sandbox?** While you develop, yes, anywhere, with the scouting logins. Test runs
and scored runs always run in our sandbox.

**Why is my run still queued?** Runs share the sandboxes in a fair order: scored runs first, then teams take turns,
the team with the fewest runs in flight first. Your team runs up to 5 test runs at a time and can have up to 3
waiting; the next waits while other teams' runs start. The run page says how many runs are ahead of yours, and
`atira test-run --follow` prints it. See [the run queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue).

# Fair play

**Rules at a glance**

You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.

**Not allowed**

- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.

**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.

The details follow.

## Allowed

- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
  amount of tokens.
  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
  for SDK configuration.
- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
  contexts inside them as you like.

## Not allowed

- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
  rules you may use.
- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.

## How it is checked

- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its
  result stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it
  marked "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Notes and docs addressed to the reviewer are not evidence of compliance
  and do not count against you on their own. Instructions trying to steer the reviewer's verdict do.
  The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers: your team reads "Flagged by the reviewing agent" or "Rejected by
  the reviewing agent". Someone from Atira looks at flagged packages shortly and unflags a misdetection; if you think
  a reject is one, contact the Atira team.
- **The organizers decide flagged packages, and can look at any submission:** they pass it, add an internal note
  (this changes nothing you or the leaderboard see) or disqualify it. A disqualified submission and its runs read
  "disqualified": it leaves the leaderboard and the final run, its runs still going stop, and your team page shows the
  organizers' reason.
- **Hardcoded values:** the reviewer rejects copied scenario values in code or config, even in defaults or fallbacks.
- **The final run** uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a
  supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software,
  with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently
  across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. That run weighs most when we pick the
  winners, so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.
- **The sandbox** reaches only our API and the websites, so every model call passes the proxy and is measured.
  Your team secrets reach only the timed run step and are redacted from its logs.
- **Website logins** exist only for a live run and stop working when it ends.
- **Browsers:** the sandbox stops any browser your agent starts beyond the ones it asked for and notes it in the
----

In PowerShell, the second line is `atira scout --env --port 8777 | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`. The proxy also
prints the command with its actual port, including when `--port 0` lets the operating system choose one.

`scout` needs no sign-in for the logins. It prints the logins the organizers published, how long they are valid,
and what happens to an answer: these are demo logins, so an answer entered on the website that takes it is
acknowledged without counting. For RFQ, a bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting. `--json` prints what
`GET /v1/challenges/<id>/scouting` returns: the logins as `access`, plus `submission`, `brief` and `answer_schema`,
shaped like a run's `/v1/runs/current`. `--env` prints:

| Variable | Value |
---
## Scouting: the public websites, without a run

Develop your agent on your own machine against the public websites, then test it in the sandbox. The scouting
logins the organizers publish need no credential:

```sh
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting"
```

It returns `challenge_id`, `challenge_version`, `scenario_id`, `expires_at`, `until_revoked`, `access` (each
website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`: the JSON a run gets as `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`), `submission`, `brief`,
`answer_schema` and a `note`: the run's own fields from `/v1/runs/current`, minus anything tied to a run token. Before
the organizers publish logins it answers `404`. These are demo logins without a run token: your agent calls its model
with your own key, and nothing done with them counts. A bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without
counting. `atira scout --env` prints the logins as shell exports and, where the organizers host models, their
base URLs on `atira models proxy`, the local proxy that signs each call for you ([CLI guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)).

## The current run

With the run token, inside the sandbox (`$CHALLENGE_API_URL` and `$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`):

## Scored run

Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset (RFQ's `public-1`) and is scored; that run
ranks on the leaderboard. The final run at the end of the hackathon uses the same sandbox on a private dataset (see
[Submitting](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md#what-happens-next)). Runs are created from your uploaded package. The sandbox is
a Linux VM with a desktop at 1280×800, a **headful Chromium** already open with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on
`127.0.0.1:9222` (or up to four, see [Browsers](#browsers)) and these toolchains, ready for your user:

- **TypeScript and JavaScript:** Node 24 (runs `.ts` files directly), npm, pnpm and bun.
- **Python:** Python 3.12 and uv (`uv venv`, `uv pip install`, `uv run`); there is no system pip.
- **Rust:** stable Rust (1.99) with cargo. Fetch crates during setup; the run is offline except for the platform
  and the websites.
- gcc, make, git, curl and jq.

1. **Setup (not counted toward your time, up to 5 minutes):** your `setup` command runs with network access but without any credentials, e.g. to install dependencies.
2. **Model warm-up (not counted toward your time):** the models the platform hosts itself, when it offers any, scale
   to zero when nobody uses them, and waking one takes one to eight minutes. The platform wakes them as soon as your
   run leaves the queue and starts your run only once they're warm (at most 10 minutes after setup), so a cold start
   never counts toward your time. The run's log says when they're warm. While runs are active, the platform keeps
   them warm. `"models"` in `agent.json` lists the ones your agent system calls, by their `provider` id from
   `GET /v1/models/status` (the start page shows it too); the run waits for those alone, and `"models": []` starts it
   right after setup:

   ```json
   {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": []}
   ```

   Without it the run waits for every hosted model. Anything else, such as an unknown id, rejects the package with
   `Invalid agent.json: models: …` and the ids it takes. It decides only the wait: your run may call any hosted model
   whatever it lists, but one it didn't list may still be waking.

   **If a hosted model fails mid-run:** retry failed calls, as with any provider; a short outage is yours to ride out.
   If our models were down for most of the run (from the first failed call on, a 5xx from our model or a lost
   connection to it, at least 8 in 10 of the run's hosted-model calls failed, over at least half its time) and the run
   then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count toward ranking or
   any limit, and a scored run starts again once by itself. A
   run that answered keeps its result.
3. **Run (timed):** your `run` command starts with this environment. The clock starts here.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the API; read your task at `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | the run token |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON: the same as `access` |
| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
| `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`, `<MODEL>_API_KEY` | for each model the platform hosts (`GET /v1/models/status`; the start page names them): its base URL through the proxy, under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>`, and the run token as its key |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google`; set the Gemini SDK's HTTP base URL explicitly as above |
| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral`, `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
| your [team secrets](#team-secrets) | for example `OPENAI_API_KEY` with your own key |
| `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222`, browser 1 |
| `CDP_URLS` | every browser's CDP URL in order, as a JSON array: `["http://127.0.0.1:9222"]` for one browser |
| `BROWSER_COUNT` | how many browsers the sandbox started: `1` unless `agent.json` asks for more |
| `DISPLAY` | `:1`, browser 1's screen; browser n is on `:n` |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` (and lowercase) | `http://127.0.0.1:3128`, the only way out of the sandbox |
| `NO_PROXY` | `localhost,127.0.0.1` (CDP stays local) |

The platform sets no API key variables of its own, except the run-token placeholder for a provider the
organizers pay for (above). `setup` runs first, with network (install your dependencies there) but without the
run's variables or your team secrets, and nothing it starts survives into the run. The run itself reaches only our API and the challenge's websites,
through that proxy; Chromium is already configured to use it. A scored run of RFQ has 20 minutes; a run that
ends without an answer scores 0.

**Why did my answer get a 400?** It does not match `answer_schema`. The response lists the issues; the run is
still open, so fix it and send it again.

**Can I run my agent outside the sandbox?** While you develop, yes, anywhere, with the scouting logins. Test runs
and scored runs always run in our sandbox.

**Why is my run still queued?** Runs share the sandboxes in a fair order: scored runs first, then teams take turns,
the team with the fewest runs in flight first. Your team runs up to 5 test runs at a time and can have up to 3
----
You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.

**Not allowed**

- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.

**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.

The details follow.

## Allowed

- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
  amount of tokens.
  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
  for SDK configuration.
- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
  contexts inside them as you like.

## Not allowed

- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
  rules you may use.
- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.

## How it is checked

- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an

# Prepare a tender response

You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way

    context: BrowserContext
    trace: Trace
    pages: list[Page] = field(default_factory=list)
    events: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # what the helpers did since the model last looked
    view: str = ""
    lock: asyncio.Lock = field(default_factory=asyncio.Lock)
    stamp: int = 0
    logins: int = 0
    seen: str = ""  # every view's text this session, to check notes against

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return self.site["siteId"]

    @property
    def page(self) -> Page:
        open_pages = [p for p in self.pages if not p.is_closed()]
        self.pages = open_pages
        return open_pages[-1]

    async def start(self) -> str:
        """Open the site's start page in a new tab, signed in."""
        await self.context.add_init_script(AUTO_CLOSE_JS)
        page = await self.context.new_page()
        self._watch(page)
        await self._goto(self.site["url"])
        return await self.look()

    def _watch(self, page: Page) -> None:
        self.pages.append(page)
        page.on("dialog", self._on_dialog)
        page.on("popup", self._on_popup)

    def _on_popup(self, popup: Page) -> None:
        self._watch(popup)
        self.events.append(f"a new window opened ({popup.url}); you are now in it, it closes back to the last one")

    async def _on_dialog(self, dialog: Dialog) -> None:
        self.events.append(f"browser {dialog.type} said: {dialog.message!r}; accepted")
        await dialog.accept()

    async def _goto(self, url: str) -> None:
        try:
            await self.page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=30000)
        except Exception as error:  # a slow load event still leaves a usable page
            self.events.append(f"navigation was slow or failed: {str(error).splitlines()[0][:160]}")
        await self.settle()

    async def settle(self) -> None:
        """Let the page finish, then run the generic helpers until nothing changes."""
        page = self.page
        self.logins = 0  # a timeout later in the run may need a fresh sign-in
        for _ in range(6):
            try:
                await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=15000)
                await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle", timeout=2500)
            except Exception:
                pass
            if (await self._safely(self._login, page) or await self._safely(self._cookies, page)
                    or await self._safely(self._error_page, page) or await self._safely(self._human_check, page)):
                page = self.page
                continue
            break
        await self._collect_closed(page)

    async def _safely(self, helper, page: Page) -> bool:
        """A helper that fails (a slow page, a detached element) just did nothing; the model sees the page as is."""
        try:

"""
Observe-only: two separate browser contexts sign in with the scouting login and read the bid wizard page and
the webmail list. Never clicks inside the wizard; never requests a TAN.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/EHL_Finale/error404ai_ehl_finals/agent")
from browser_tools import SiteSession  # noqa: E402
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright  # noqa: E402
from tracing import Trace  # noqa: E402

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SCOUT = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, "scout.json")))
SITES = {a["siteId"]: a for a in SCOUT["access"]}
REF = re.search(r"\((VG-[0-9-]+)\)", SCOUT["brief"]).group(1)
PHASE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "observe"


async def text(page, limit=2500):
    try:
        body = await page.locator("body").inner_text(timeout=8000)
    except Exception as e:
        return f"<no text: {e}>"
    return re.sub(r"\n\s*\n+", "\n", body)[:limit]


async def form_values(page):
    return await page.evaluate("""() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('input,select,textarea'))
      .filter(e => e.type !== 'hidden' && e.offsetParent !== null)
      .map(e => `${e.name||e.id||e.type}=${e.type==='checkbox'||e.type==='radio' ? e.checked : e.value}`)""")


async def open_site(ctx, site_id, path, label):
    s = SiteSession(site=SITES[site_id], context=ctx, trace=Trace(None))
    await s.start()
    if path:
        await s._goto(SITES[site_id]["url"] + path)
    page = s.page
    cookies = sorted(c["name"] for c in await ctx.cookies())
    print(f"\n===== {label} {site_id} url={page.url} cookies={cookies}")
    print("fields:", await form_values(page))
    print(await text(page))
    return s


async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        a = await browser.new_context()
        b = await browser.new_context()
        sub = f"/tenders/{REF}/submission"
        sa = await open_site(a, "tender-portal", sub, "A")
        if PHASE == "step1":
            await step1(sa)
            await sa._goto(SITES["tender-portal"]["url"] + sub)
            print("\n===== A after step 1, reloaded:", sa.page.url)
            print("fields:", await form_values(sa.page))
            print(await text(sa.page, 1500))
        await open_site(b, "tender-portal", sub, "B")
        if PHASE == "observe":
            ma = await open_site(a, "mail", None, "A")
            mb = await open_site(b, "mail", None, "B")
            for s in (ma, mb):
                print("mail page", s.page.url)
        await browser.close()


async def step1(s):
    """Fill only the bidder data the brief states, then the step's own continue button."""
    page = s.page
    company = page.get_by_label(re.compile("firma|unternehmen|name", re.I)).first
    vat = page.get_by_label(re.compile("ust|umsatzsteuer|vat", re.I)).first
    await company.fill("Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH")
    await vat.fill("DE811234567")
    btn = page.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("weiter|speichern|übernehmen", re.I)).first
    print("step1 button:", await btn.inner_text())
    await btn.click()
    await s.settle()


asyncio.run(main())

content.text:
## Isolated state on the challenge sites: findings

The platform gives teams no isolated scouting state, but most of it isn't needed: the bid wizard is already private to each browser session. The only shared state is the webmail, which holds the TAN mails.

**1. What the docs and API offer: nothing per team.**
- `api.md`: scouting returns "the logins the organizers publish… These are demo logins without a run token… nothing done with them counts." The response has `until_revoked: true` and never expires.
- The OpenAPI spec has no reset endpoint, no extra accounts and no per-team scouting. The only related endpoint is `POST /v1/challenges/{id}/practice-runs`, marked "Deprecated and internal: organizers' demo access… participants never need it" (llms-full: "Organizers only"). I did not call it.
- `faq.md`: "Can I run my agent outside the sandbox? While you develop, yes, anywhere, with the scouting logins."
- The two announcements say nothing about this. One raised concurrent test runs to 4, but our learned.md says 5; worth checking.

**2. Experiment (two separate headless browser contexts, no other agent running):**
- **Bid wizard: tied to the session cookie, not the account.** Fresh contexts A and B both opened an empty step 1 (Bieterdaten). A filled in the bidder data once (the brief's company name and VAT id, plus the mailbox address read from the webmail) and pressed Weiter. After a reload, A showed step 2 (Angebotsart) and B still showed an empty step 1. The leftover state we saw earlier came from reusing our own session.
- **Webmail: one mailbox shared by everyone.** Both contexts saw exactly the same list: 66 messages, the newest being TAN mails numbered "Anforderung 66, 65, 64…". So the TAN mails and their numbering are shared across all teams.
- **Untested:** whether one TAN request cancels TANs requested from other sessions, because I was not allowed to request one. The shared numbering and the jumps we saw make account-wide cancellation likely.

**3. Using a test run's logins from my laptop: technically possible, not advisable. I did not try it.**
- A past test run's log shows the same public hostnames as scouting (`atira-rfq-*.kyora.run`). Runs get separate logins on the same public sites, so they would probably be reachable from outside.
- The rules work against it:
  - run-contract: "Site logins are issued per run and only work while that run is live."
  - fair-play forbids "trying to get data out of the sandbox" and says "Nobody helps it during a run."
- Our own agent would also share those accounts while the run is live, and code that prints `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` is exactly what the package reviewer flags.
- Recommendation: don't do it without written permission from the organizers.

## Options, best first

1. **Use the session isolation we already have (no risk).** Run the bid form locally up to step 6, in separate browser contexts per developer. Add a stop before the TAN request, and test TAN signing only in test runs (up to 4–5 at once).
2. **Ask the organizers (one message, low risk).** Ask for per-team scouting logins or a mailbox reset, and whether using a live test run's logins from outside is allowed. Mention that TAN requests from different teams collide in the shared mailbox.
3. **Read the TAN by request number right after our own request.** This keeps local signing mostly working, but we still cancel other teams' TANs and they cancel ours. Use it sparingly.
4. **Leak a test run's logins to a laptop (not recommended).** It risks a fair-play violation and collides with our own running agent.

I appended one bullet with these results to `docs/learned.md` and committed nothing. The probe script and its logs are in `/Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/064ce75e/tmp/iso/`: `observe.py`, `obs1.log` and `obs2.log`.
